editorial:
Imagine you are just trying to survive high school without ruining your social life, but then you end up in a massive lie that spirals out of control. That is exactly what happens here. You follow two best friends who decide to pretend they are trans women to cover up some embarrassing mistakes before graduation. It starts off as a wild, chaotic prank, but it quickly turns into something way more meaningful. The vibe is light and funny, but it also has a lot of heart as you watch these characters navigate a world they do not fully understand while trying to keep their secret safe from their classmates.

The acting is the best part, especially seeing the lead character transition from joking around to realizing that this fake persona is actually who they are inside. The pacing is quick, so you never feel bored, though some of the jokes are a bit predictable. If you want a feel-good story that makes you laugh and cry, you should definitely check this out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality, or if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great call.
endingExplained: In the final act, the truth comes out during the graduation ceremony in front of the whole school. While one friend admits the whole thing was a prank and asks for forgiveness, the other friend stands their ground. They realize they are actually a trans woman and decide to live their truth openly. The movie ends with them staying best friends and the main character starting their new life with confidence and support.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and comedies with a lot of heart.
